newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Independent says '97 began reasonably well.
newsitem.headline: Independent says '97 began reasonably well.

text.p: Independent Newspapers Plc chairman Tony O'Reilly said on Wednesday that 1997 had started "reasonably well" and he hoped for a "good increase" in annual operating profits.

"1997 has started reasonably well and we hope that with the inclusion of New Zealand for a full year we will have a good increase in operating profit," O'Reilly told shareholders at the Irish-based media company's annual meeting.
Independent took an 85-percent stake in New Zealand's Wilson and Horton in 1996.
O'Reilly said Independent's wide variety of companies and brands in several countries "promise well for the future long-term growth of the international company".
But he said competition was strong.

"The competition both from our direct competitors and from new markets such as digital TV and new ways of securing news and entertainment in an age which is increasingly audiovisual make our markets worldwide fiercely competitive," he told shareholders.
